articles.title: Blackburn angler's 52kg carp catch hailed as world record
articles.summary: Ash Hegarty says his late dad would be "proud" of his huge catch.
articles.body:
An angler from Lancashire has landed a carp being hailed as a new world record after travelling to a lake in Hungary.

Ash Hegarty, from Blackburn, caught a 52kg (114lb 10oz) common carp and said landing the fish was "indescribable".

Photographs and videos of the catch have been shared widely online, with Hegarty receiving calls from German and Swedish journalists.

Hegarty said: "I'm just an ordinary lad from Blackburn who loves fishing, and somehow I've found myself at the centre of a story being shared around the world after catching what is being described as a new world-record carp."

"If there's one thing I wish I could do right now, it would be to pick up the phone and tell my dad. I know how proud he would have been," he said.

Hegarty, who travelled more than 1,300 miles (2,092km) to Euro Aqua Lake, shared the moment with his older brother, Nigel.

The 32-year-old said their late father had introduced them to fishing when they were young and the pair had continued to fish together ever since.

"Fishing for us is a break from business and a break from life," he said. "When we go fishing, we literally switch off. Whether we're there for one night or five nights, it's good for your mental health and your soul."

The brothers made the journey to the lake, which is renowned among anglers for producing some of the world's largest carp.

Hegarty said he had been resting beside the water when an alarm sounded from one of his rods.

He said his legs were trembling as he realised he had hooked the huge fish and spent about 20 minutes bringing it in.

"It was slow and heavy," he said. "When I finally saw the size of it, everyone started gathering round. It was like a car tyre in the net."

As photographs of the carp were shared online, Hegarty said his phone "hasn't stopped ringing", with messages arriving from around the world.

"I know how proud my dad would have been," he said. "To do it with my brother beside me made it even more special."

articles.title: BBC Weather Watcher shortlisted for Royal Meteorological Society photography award
articles.summary: Rachel Cassidy's picture - A Midsummer Night’s Dream - captures a display of noctilucent clouds.
articles.body:
A BBC Weather Watcher who regularly shares her photographs with the organisation has been shortlisted for a prestigious international photography award.

Rachel Cassidy is the only photographer from Northern Ireland to reach the final shortlist of the Royal Meteorological Society's Weather (RMetS) Photographer of the Year 2026 competition.

Her photograph, A Midsummer Night's Dream , captures a display of noctilucent clouds above Binevenagh and Lough Foyle on the north coast.

The image was selected from more than 5,500 entries submitted by photographers around the world.

Rachel, from Limavady, is a familiar contributor to BBC weather output, often sharing images of changing skies and landscapes through BBC Weather Watchers.

Rachel's shortlisted image captures one of the more unusual sights in the summer night sky.

Noctilucent clouds - sometimes known as night-shining clouds – form around 80km (50 miles) above Earth's surface, much higher than ordinary weather clouds.

They are made up of tiny ice crystals and can be seen glowing against the dark sky when they are illuminated by sunlight from below the horizon.

They are most commonly spotted during the summer months at higher latitudes, particularly around twilight.

Rachel said reaching the final shortlist was particularly special because of her love of the weather and the area she calls home.

"It feels like a pinch-me moment, it was really quite surreal when I found out I had been shortlisted," Rachel told BBC News NI.

"Being able to capture something so spectacular from my own garden, in our part of the world we call home, was just great."

However, photographing the spectacle was not as easy as you might think.

"It was tricky to capture because noctilucent clouds are quite unpredictable, you often have to be in the right place at the right time," she said.

"I remember being in the garden and seeing it happen. I just grabbed my phone as the colours got more vivid and bright - it was like an ocean moving in the sky."

Rachel said it would be amazing to showcase Northern Ireland if she won the competition.

"I'm a big fan of the weather, and to win against so many fantastic photographers will be another pinch me moment," she said.

Now in its 11th year, the RMetS competition celebrates photographs that capture the beauty, power and impact of weather and climate around the world.

This year's 30 shortlisted photographs feature scenes from 13 countries, ranging from dramatic lightning strikes and spectacular cloud formations to wildfires and flooding.

Prizes range from £1,500 to £50 and the winners will be announced on 17 November.

articles.title: Enem em Macapá: incentivo escolar garante entrada sem atrasos | G1
articles.standfirst: Trabalho de conscientização feito pela Escola Sebastiana Lenir refletiu em entrada tranquila na capital. Exame segue cronograma oficial do horário de Brasília.
articles.summary: Enem em Macapá: mobilização de professores e lembretes em redes sociais garantiram portões sem correria e pontualidade dos candidatos no primeiro dia de provas.
articles.body:
Enem 2026 em Macapá. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

A abertura e o fechamento dos portões na Escola Estadual Sebastiana Lenir de Almeida, em Macapá , ocorreram sem registros de correria no primeiro dia do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio ( Enem ), neste domingo (8).

Antes da abertura dos portões, estudantes já aguardavam a entrada no local munidos de lanches e documentos, enquanto vendedores ambulantes aproveitavam a movimentação para vender canetas pretas de tubo transparente na frente da instituição.

A pontualidade dos candidatos foi reflexo direto de uma preparação que começou meses antes do exame. Segundo o professor de Artes Hugo Barbosa Santos, a equipe pedagógica organizou uma rede de apoio presencial e virtual para orientar os alunos sobre prazos, locais de prova e a importância da antecedência.

"Fizemos uma campanha bem firme de incentivo, sempre citando a importância desse exame nacional, de que é uma oportunidade para a vida deles ingressar numa graduação em ensino superior. Compartilhamos orientações nos grupos de WhatsApp e em sala de aula para que eles verificassem o local de prova com antecedência", afirmou o professor.

Professor de Artes da Escola Estadual Sebastiana Lenir, Hugo Barbosa Santos. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Santos ressaltou que a mobilização evitou incidentes na entrada. "A maioria dos alunos chegou antes da abertura dos portões. Não tivemos candidatos chegando correndo ou atrasados, foi uma entrada bem tranquila", completou.

Nataly Evelin dos Santos, de 17 anos, no Enem . Moradora da comunidade Corre Água, na região do Pacuí, a estudante da Escola Estadual São João viajou até Macapá para fazer a prova pela primeira vez

"Desejo que todos alcancem seus objetivos, porque é um esforço muito grande para estarmos aqui. O Enem é muito importante para nós do interior, pois é a forma de ingressar em uma boa faculdade", declarou a jovem.

Nataly Evelin dos Santos, de 17 anos, faz o Enem pela primeira vez. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Uma das novidades desta edição é a integração do Enem com o Sistema de Avaliação da Educação Básica (Saeb), determinada pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC). Com a mudança, a participação e o desempenho dos alunos na prova também serão computados para compor o índice educacional do estado.

Além disso, uma portaria publicada pelo MEC validou os dois domingos de aplicação do Enem como dias letivos na rede pública.

Todas as etapas da prova seguem estritamente o horário oficial de Brasília. No Amapá , o cronograma de aplicação ocorre nos seguintes horários:

Saída permitida (sem caderno de questões)15h30

Saída permitida (com caderno de questões)18h30

Após o fechamento dos portões, às 13h, não é permitida a entrada de nenhum candidato. Entre 13h e 13h30, os estudantes passam por procedimentos de segurança e vistoria nas salas.

Escola Estadual Sebastiana Lenir, em Macapá. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Empreendedores aproveitaram a oportunidade para a venda de canetas. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

articles.title: Defesa Civil: kit de emergência é preventivo e não causa pânico | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgão fez nova publicação após forte reação na internet sobre orientações de prevenção para "grandes desastres".
articles.summary: Defesa Civil Nacional reforça que orientações sobre o kit de emergência são preventivas, após postagens sobre grandes desastres gerarem pânico nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil Nacional fez uma nova postagem nas redes sociais neste domingo (8) afirmando que falar de kit de emergência não é sinal de perigo, mas "sinal de que prevenir faz parte da rotina".

Post da defesa civil após forte reação nas redes sociais às orientações de como montar um kit de emergência para 72 horas — Foto: Reprodução/X

A publicação foi feita dois dias depois que o órgão compartilhou instruções de como preparar um kit de emergência para "desastres de grande proporções".

Instruções da Defesa Civil para kit de emergência publicadas nas redes sociais em 6 de novembro — Foto: Reprodução/X

Na nova publicação, a Defesa Civil nacional afirma que o perfil posta diariamente sobre prevenção, e que publicou conteúdos sobre kits de emergência nos dias 16 de março e 3 de abril. "Orientações são postadas sempre que necessário", diz uma das imagens do post. "Informação e preparação trazem mais tranquilidade".

Já na postagem anterior, a Defesa Civil deu instruções sobre como preparar um kit de emergência. "Em situações de grandes desastres, as equipes de socorro podem levar mais tempo para chegar. Por isso, é importante estar preparado para as primeiras 72 horas", diz parte da postagem.

O órgão deu orientação para o público reunir água potável, comida não perecível, utensílios e itens de primeiros socorros e de higiene, roupas, eletrônicos como rádio e lanternas, documentos pessoas e sacolas plásticas avulsas.

Na semana passada, diferentes países europeus como Reino Unido, Dinamarca, Alemanha, Noruega e França orientaram seus cidadãos a manter reservas de itens essenciais em casa para se sustentar por até 72 horas. O Reino Unido, por exemplo, lançou a camapanha "Be Ready" (Esteja preparado), que foi alvo de desinformação nas redes sociais.

Com isso, a publicação da Defesa Civil chamou atenção e as pessoas reagiram nas redes. Enquanto alguns usuários comentaram que o conteúdo era um "exagero", outros citaram desastres climáticos. Alguns reagiram escrevendo que "alguma coisa vai acontecer".

O g1 entrou em contato com o Ministério da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional, responsável pela Defesa Civil, para perguntar por que a primeira postagem foi feita ao mesmo tempo em que países europeus davam orientações parecidas sobre kits de emergência.

Em resposta, o ministério afirmou que a Secretaria Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil divulga "regularmente" orientações de autoproteção para diferentes situações de emergência. "Entre essas orientações estão recomendações de como agir em diferentes situações de riscos e a organização de um kit doméstico de emergência".

articles.summary: Após o grave acidente em Barra Mansa que vitimou dez pessoas na localidade de Ataulfo de Paiva, prefeitura decreta luto e hasteia bandeiras a meio-mastro.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Barra Mansa — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Barra Mansa

A Prefeitura de Barra Mansa (RJ) decretou luto oficial de três dias após o acidente que matou dez pessoas na madruga deste domingo (8) na Estrada Fazenda Santa Catarina, na localidade Ataulfo de Paiva.

Segundo a prefeitura, durante o período, as bandeiras do município ficarão hasteadas a meio-mastro em todos os órgãos e repartições públicas.

Ainda de acordo com o órgão, o decreto entra em vigor a partir deste domingo (8).

Em nota, a prefeitura informou o luto e se solidarizou com os familiares e amigos das vítimas.

Confira a nota da Prefeitura de Barra Mansa na íntegra.

"CONSIDERANDO o sentimento de solidariedade, dor e respeito pelas recentes perdas humanas, inclusive de crianças.

Art. 1 - Fica decretado luto oficial de 3 (três) dias, contados a partir da data de publicação deste Decreto, em todo o território do Município de Barra Mansa, em sinal de profundo pesar.

​Art. 2 - Durante o período de luto determinado por este Decreto, as bandeiras do município ficarão hasteadas a meio-mastro em todos os órgãos e repartições públicas municipais.

Art. 3 - Este Decreto entra em vigor na data de sua publicação"

articles.title: Can Netanyahu stage a comeback in Israel? What if Eisenkot fails to form government
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has been given the first opportunity to form the next government after President Isaac Herzog invited him
articles.body: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has been given the first opportunity to form the next government after President Isaac Herzog invited him on Saturday. The inconclusive October 27 election failed to give any party a clear parliamentary majority.However, with his coalition falling short of the numbers needed to govern, Eisenkot faces several challenges.He has options laid out to form a minority government. He can secure support from Arab parties, reach an understanding with ultra-Orthodox factions or explore a broader unity arrangement.But if he fails within the 42-day deadline, the incumbent Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could get another chance to form a government.Eisenkot's Yashar party and its potential allies have 48 seats in the 120-member parliament.While his seats fall short of the 61-seat majority mark required, support from Israel's two Arab parties, which together hold 19 seats, could help his bloc reach 67. The parties could support his government from outside without formally joining the coalition, allowing Eisenkot to attempt a minority government.How Eisenkot can form a minority governmentOne possibility is for Eisenkot to bring together his natural allies, including the centre-right Together party, The Democrats and Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home. Their combined strength stands at 48 seats.The two Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, could then provide outside support. Both have endorsed Eisenkot to form the next government and expressed willingness to work with his broader camp to prevent Netanyahu's return to power.However, this arrangement faces political hurdles. Eisenkot had pledged during his campaign not to include Arab parties in his government. Reversing that position could prove difficult, particularly after the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack hardened attitudes towards Israel's Arab minority.Lieberman has also repeatedly ruled out forming a minority government with Arab parties. So far, only The Democrats, a centre-left party, have publicly supported their inclusion.Netanyahu has also focused his campaign on delegitimising any government that relies on Arab support.There is a precedent for such an arrangement. Ra'am joined former prime minister Naftali Bennett's government in 2021. Bennett, who now heads the Together party, is among Eisenkot's potential partners. However, that government collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.Can ultra-Orthodox parties give Eisenkot a majorityAnother option is to seek support from Israel's two ultra-Orthodox parties, which together hold 13 seats. Their backing could take Eisenkot's bloc to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government.However, reaching an agreement will not be easy. The main sticking point is military service exemptions traditionally granted to ultra-Orthodox seminary students. The exemptions have drawn criticism from many Israelis who believe the burden of military service is unfairly placed on the wider population.Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have strongly opposed these exemptions. However, Lieberman signalled some flexibility on Friday, saying he was open to a compromise."You cannot have it all", he told supporters.The two ultra-Orthodox parties have also taken different positions following the election. United Torah Judaism declined to endorse any candidate, while Shas backed Netanyahu.What happens if Eisenkot failsEisenkot has up to 42 days to form a government. If he cannot secure the necessary support, Herzog is likely to invite Netanyahu to make another attempt.Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc has been reduced from its original 64 seats to 53. Despite this, the prime minister could try to weaken the opposition by persuading lawmakers from rival parties to defect and join his camp.He has used this strategy before. In the run-up to the 2022 election, Netanyahu managed to destabilise the government he was opposing by drawing support away from its ranks. However, the opposition bloc at the time had a much narrower lead, meaning fewer defections were needed to bring it down.If Netanyahu gets another opportunity, he would need to find enough support to rebuild a parliamentary majority.Could a unity government emergeIf Eisenkot cannot form a government with Arab or ultra-Orthodox support, another possibility is a unity arrangement involving his Yashar party, Together, Israel Our Home and Netanyahu's Likud.Likud emerged as the largest party in the October 27 election with 27 seats. A grouping involving these parties would command 67 seats, giving it a parliamentary majority.However, this appears unlikely for now. Eisenkot and his partners would have to abandon their central campaign promise of removing Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu, in turn, would likely have to distance himself from his traditional far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies.Still, prolonged coalition negotiations or renewed fighting with Iran could push the rival camps towards a unity arrangement.Could Israel face another electionIf both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form a government, parliament can nominate another candidate. The process has a deadline of around 100 days. If no candidate succeeds, Israel will have to hold another election.Herzog has already warned against another vote. articles.title: Watch: Shattered glass, scattered books after strong earthquake rattles Japan
articles.summary: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured,
articles.body: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.The quake, which struck at 1:04 am, was located about 40 kilometres below the earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. articles.title: Is Netanyahu's time up? 10 things to know as rival Gadi Eisenkot gets shot at power in Israel
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government after the October 27 election failed
articles.body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government after the October 27 election failed to produce a clear parliamentary majority. It has given Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main challenger the first opportunity to take power.Eisenkot, a former chief of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), secured recommendations from lawmakers representing 67 of the Knesset's 120 members.However, forming a coalition remains a challenge, as his bloc lacks a confirmed majority and potential partners disagree over the role of Arab parties and ultra-Orthodox factions. Netanyahu, whose Likud remains the largest party, is meanwhile pushing for a national unity government.Here are 10 things to know about the political developments in Israel.1. Eisenkot gets six weeks to form Israel's next governmentHerzog announced his decision on Saturday after consultations with representatives of political parties and separate discussions with Eisenkot and Netanyahu. The mandate gives the former military chief up to 42 days to negotiate with potential partners and secure the parliamentary support needed to form a government.The decision marks a significant setback for Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, whose attempt to retain power suffered a blow after most parliamentary factions recommended Eisenkot for the post.In his first reaction, Eisenkot called for a national emergency government. "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," he wrote on X.2. How Eisenkot secured backing of 67 lawmakersEisenkot received recommendations from factions representing 67 lawmakers in the 120-member Knesset. These included the Jewish-led opposition bloc, which holds 48 seats, Arab party Ra'am with eight seats and the Joint List with 11 seats.The Joint List's unanimous endorsement proved crucial in taking Eisenkot past the 61-seat threshold needed for a parliamentary majority.Netanyahu, meanwhile, received recommendations from factions representing 46 lawmakers. Seven lawmakers did not endorse either candidate.However, the recommendations do not automatically translate into a governing coalition. Eisenkot must still negotiate with potential partners and secure their support on key policy issues.3. Arab parties could determine whether Eisenkot forms a governmentThe backing of Ra'am and the Joint List has given Eisenkot an important advantage. Their combined 19 seats could help him secure a majority, but working with the Arab-led parties presents a political challenge.An Arab party has been part of an Israeli governing coalition only once before. Ra'am joined the government led by former prime minister Naftali Bennett in 2021. That administration collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.Eisenkot could form a minority government with his natural allies, including Together, The Democrats and Israel Our Home, while relying on the Arab parties for external support. Such an arrangement would give the broader grouping 67 seats.However, Avigdor Lieberman's Israel Our Home has repeatedly ruled out supporting a minority government backed by Arab parties. Only The Democrats has publicly called for their inclusion.The political sensitivities have also intensified following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the subsequent war in Gaza.4. Ultra-Orthodox parties offer another possible route to a majorityEisenkot and his partners could also approach Israel's two ultra-Orthodox parties, which collectively hold 13 seats. Their support could help the opposition bloc reach the 61-seat majority without relying on Arab parties.However, negotiations could run into disagreements over military service exemptions traditionally granted to ultra-Orthodox seminary students.Eisenkot and Lieberman have strongly criticised these exemptions. Many Israelis believe the arrangements place an unfair burden on other citizens who serve in the military.United Torah Judaism declined to endorse either candidate during the presidential consultations, while Shas backed Netanyahu. This leaves the possibility of an agreement open, but any deal would require difficult compromises.5. Eisenkot wants a national emergency government with four key principlesEisenkot has pitched a national emergency government to address Israel's political and security challenges. His proposed administration would be guided by four principles: recognising Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, upholding the Declaration of Independence, ensuring universal national and military conscription, and dismantling Hamas' military and political wings.His party, Yashar, has also indicated that it would only work with parties and lawmakers who accept its principles.In a statement responding to Netanyahu's appeal for a unity government, Yashar urged Likud members to distance themselves from what it described as an alliance with "radical parties", apparently referring to the far-right factions in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc.6. Netanyahu loses his parliamentary majority, but Likud remains the largest partyDespite the setback, Netanyahu remains a significant force in Israeli politics. His Likud party emerged as the largest single party in the October 27 election, securing 27 seats.However, his religious-nationalist bloc has fallen from its original 64 seats to 53, leaving it short of the 61 required for a parliamentary majority.The prime minister also suffered a setback when United Torah Judaism refused to endorse him during consultations with Herzog. The party's decision has raised questions about the stability of his long-standing political alliance with ultra-Orthodox factions.7. Netanyahu calls for a national unity government to counter Eisenkot's bidFollowing Eisenkot's appointment, Netanyahu called for the immediate formation of a broad national unity government comprising all Zionist political factions.In a televised address, he argued that Israel needed a united political leadership to address external security threats, particularly from Iran.The proposed government, Netanyahu said, would "permanently remove the nuclear threat from Iran, preserve Israel as a Jewish state, and bring unity among us".However, the opposition rejected his appeal. Democratic Party chairman Yair Golan said Netanyahu's government must be replaced by a "government of salvation and change" to protect Israel's democracy, security and future.Golan also called for ultra-Orthodox citizens to be conscripted into the military and integrated into the workforce. He argued that the burden of defence and taxation should not fall disproportionately on secular Israelis.8. Netanyahu seeks to prevent Eisenkot from joining hands with Arab partiesA key part of Netanyahu's political strategy has been to discourage any arrangement between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties.He has repeatedly portrayed their participation in government as a national security threat. Shortly before Herzog announced his decision, Netanyahu warned against "hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters", a description he uses for the Arab-led parties.He has also made unsubstantiated claims that Arab parties "stole" the elections.Eisenkot, meanwhile, has indicated that he could work with them under certain conditions, including their acceptance of his position that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be destroyed.The issue could become one of the biggest obstacles in Eisenkot's efforts to form a government.9. Netanyahu could get another opportunity if Eisenkot failsIf Eisenkot fails to form a government within 42 days, Herzog could give Netanyahu the next opportunity to secure a parliamentary majority.The prime minister could attempt to weaken the opposition by persuading lawmakers from rival parties to defect and join his camp.Netanyahu has used similar political manoeuvres in the past. In the run-up to the 2022 election, he managed to destabilise the coalition opposing him and eventually returned to power.However, his current challenge is more difficult because the opposition bloc has a wider base of support and he would need to attract a greater number of lawmakers to secure a majority.10. Another election remains possible if both leaders failIf neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu succeeds in forming a government, the Knesset could nominate another candidate to attempt the task.The process has a deadline of around 100 days. If no candidate manages to form a government within that period, Israel would have to hold another election.A unity government between Eisenkot's partners and Netanyahu's Likud is another possible outcome, although it appears unlikely at present. Such an arrangement would command 67 seats, but Eisenkot's allies would have to abandon their central electoral promise of removing Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu, in turn, would have to distance himself from his far-right and ultra-Orthodox political allies.Herzog has urged political parties to approach negotiations with an open mind and do everything possible to avoid another election.You use AI every day. articles.title: An elderly man fell while carrying breakfast and severed an artery; two Queensland carpenters used a dress and adhesive tape to save his life, leaving his wife overwhelmed with gratitude
articles.summary: An ordinary morning in Gracemere, Queensland, turned into a life-threatening emergency when 93-year-old Ian Barton suffered a severe wrist injury after
articles.body: An ordinary morning in Gracemere, Queensland, turned into a life-threatening emergency when 93-year-old Ian Barton suffered a severe wrist injury after falling while carrying a bowl of porridge. The bowl shattered during the fall, and a fragment sliced an artery in his wrist, causing heavy bleeding. Hearing a woman screaming for help from across the street, carpenter Josh Sander and his apprentice Gary Tunbridge abandoned their work and rushed to assist him. When a tea towel failed to control the bleeding, the two men improvised a tighter dressing using a dress and adhesive tape from their work vehicle. They continued applying pressure while waiting approximately 40 minutes for an ambulance. Barton was eventually taken to hospital, where he underwent surgery and remained in a stable condition.A morning job turns into a life-threatening emergencyThe incident occurred shortly before 8am on Monday, November 2, 2026, in a quiet cul-de-sac in Gracemere, a town near Rockhampton in central Queensland, Australia.Sander and Tunbridge were working on a pergola at a nearby property and were preparing to climb onto its roof when they heard a woman screaming for help from across the street.The woman was Joy Barton, 89, whose husband, Ian, had fallen in their backyard. The two tradesmen immediately stopped working and rushed to the property.They found the 93-year-old lying on his back patio, surrounded by blood. According to Sander's account to ABC Capricornia, Barton had tripped over the raised edge of a small ramp while carrying his breakfast. He fell onto the bowl of porridge, which shattered and caused a deep cut to his wrist.Sander initially paused when he saw the amount of blood but quickly realised that the injury had severed an artery and that the situation was potentially life-threatening."We just ripped in and weren't afraid to get a bit bloody and it's turned out for the best," Sander told ABC.Two carpenters use a dress and adhesive tape to control bleedingSander initially attempted to control the bleeding by wrapping a tea towel tightly around Barton's injured wrist. However, it did not slow the blood loss sufficiently.Realising that they needed a tighter dressing, he asked Tunbridge to retrieve adhesive tape from their work truck. Sander then went inside the house and found one of Joy Barton's dresses.The two men used the dress fabric to wrap the wound, after which Tunbridge tightly secured it with adhesive tape. They also continued applying pressure to the injury and the makeshift tourniquet in an effort to control the bleeding.Sander explained that the first attempt with the tea towel had not been sufficient, prompting him to look for something that could provide a tighter wrap.The improvised dressing became central to their efforts to keep Barton alive until emergency services arrived.Elderly man repeatedly loses consciousness during ambulance waitThe two tradesmen remained with Barton for approximately 40 minutes before paramedics reached the property.The situation remained serious throughout the wait. Sander said Barton repeatedly appeared to fade away, forcing the men to try to wake him and keep him responsive.At one point, they noticed that the elderly man appeared to be choking. Tunbridge realised that Barton's false teeth were lodged in his mouth and reached in to remove them to help keep his airway clear.Sander later recalled that his apprentice had acted quickly after noticing the problem, helping maintain the man's airflow while they waited for medical assistance.A Queensland Ambulance Service spokesperson told ABC that the local Gracemere crew was experiencing significant demand at the time but responded as quickly as possible to treat and transport the patient to hospital.The service also thanked members of the community for their quick thinking and for providing care before paramedics arrived.93-year-old undergoes surgery at Rockhampton HospitalBarton was taken to Rockhampton Hospital for treatment of his serious wrist injury. He remained in a stable condition and underwent an operation on the afternoon of the incident.His wife, Joy, later described how frightened she had been when she saw her husband being taken away by paramedics.She recalled kissing him as he was placed on the ambulance chair because she feared he might not survive.However, she was relieved to see a considerable improvement in his appearance after the operation.The family was hopeful that Barton would be able to return home within the following days. Joy said he would likely need several months of recovery at home after leaving hospital.Wife thanks tradesmen for saving her husband's lifeJoy expressed deep gratitude to Sander and Tunbridge for responding to the emergency and helping her husband before the ambulance arrived.She said she believed the two men had saved Ian's life and described them as heroes."They saved my husband's life ... I thought he was going to die," she told ABC.Joy also recalled telling her husband after his operation: "Ian, darling, that bloke saved your life."The couple have been married for more than six decades, making the incident particularly frightening for their family.Their granddaughter posted a message on social media the following day, thanking the tradesmen for helping her grandfather. The post helped bring attention to their actions and allowed the family to identify and publicly acknowledge the two men.Joy said she was still trying to work out how she could repay them for what they had done. Sander and Tunbridge, meanwhile, said they were simply relieved that Barton was recovering.Apprentice had started his carpentry career four months earlierThe incident was particularly remarkable for Tunbridge, who had begun his carpentry apprenticeship only four months before the emergency.Despite being relatively new to the trade, he worked alongside Sander to help Barton during the critical wait for medical assistance.When asked about the possibility of becoming a paramedic after the experience, Tunbridge joked that emergency medical work had not been part of his apprenticeship training and that he had no immediate plans to change careers.Sander also reflected on his first-aid knowledge, admitting that it had been several years since he last completed a first-aid course. The experience prompted him to consider booking a refresher course.The two tradesmen had been focused on an ordinary construction job that morning before the emergency across the street brought their work to an unexpected halt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Houthi attacks target Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia as explosions rock Riyadh
articles.summary: Multiple loud explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh after the country's Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert over a potential
articles.body: Multiple loud explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh after the country's Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert over a potential threat.Witnesses as per Reuters reported damage to a building belonging to oil giant Saudi Aramco in the city's financial district amid renewed hostilities with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels.A Reuters witness reported hearing several loud booms shortly after the alert was issued. The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles over Riyadh and the southern region. It also said two Houthi missiles fired towards the capital had been intercepted.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for a series of missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi oil facilities and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. He said six military operations had been carried out against strategic and military installations across the kingdom using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones.According to Saree, the attacks were launched in response to what the group described as Saudi aggression against Yemen."The first operation targeted Khalid International Airport, oil storage tanks, and a distillation tower belonging to Aramco in the Saudi enemy's capital, Riyadh, and, by Allah's grace, successfully achieved its objective," Saree said.He said the second operation targeted Aramco facilities in Khurais, while the third struck Pumping Station No. 8 in the Dawadmi area.The fourth operation, according to the spokesperson, targeted Saudi military concentrations at a National Guard camp in Najran. The fifth targeted troop positions east of Al-Jawf Governorate in three stages."The sixth operation targeted Saudi enemy troop concentrations east of Raghwah and Madghal districts in Marib Governorate, under the command of Saudi officer Fares Al-Shammari, leaving a large number of dead and wounded among their ranks," he added.Saree claimed that the operations caused several casualties among Saudi military personnel. These claims have not been independently verified.In a separate post on X, the Houthi spokesperson alleged that Saudi Arabia had carried out 105 airstrikes and missile attacks on Yemen over the preceding 24 hours, targeting areas in Sanaa and the governorates of Al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Hajjah, Saada, Marib and Lahj."These attacks left dozens of civilians dead and wounded, most of them women and children. This brings the total number of airstrikes and missile attacks by the Saudi aggressor against our country since the escalation began to 4,369," he said.Threatening further retaliation, Saree said, "We will continue our operations deep inside Saudi territory, imposing the equation of blockade for blockade and escalation for escalation, and targeting Saudi enemy troop concentrations and officers."Meanwhile, Yemen's internationally recognised government has urged Lebanon to take coordinated measures to stop Hezbollah's alleged military assistance to the Houthi militia.Yemen's Foreign Minister Afrah Al-Zouba called for cooperation between the security and intelligence agencies of the two countries to prevent further support for Houthi military operations.The renewed fighting has shattered a United Nations-brokered truce reached in 2022, which had largely halted attacks between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who control Sanaa. The group has since resumed missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi airports and oil facilities, while Riyadh has carried out airstrikes in Yemen in support of its Yemeni allies.The escalation, linked to the wider US-Iran conflict, has revived the 12-year war in Yemen, which has triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises and left the Arab world's poorest country deeply fragmented.The International Organization for Migration said in October that more than 200,000 people had been displaced since the latest round of fighting began.You use AI every day. articles.title: Brent School Street fines at one location exceed £1m
articles.summary: The council issues penalty charges totalling £1.15m over the scheme near Manor School in Kensal Rise.
articles.body:
A London council has issued more than £1m worth of penalty charge notices (PCNs) to drivers under a School Street scheme in less than two years.

Brent Council issued PCNs totalling £1.15m after introducing the scheme outside Manor School in Kensal Rise in November 2024, saying it would improve road safety and the environment.

Ward councillor Barbara Want raised concerns about the scheme and claimed that the signs were "too high and not properly visible".

Brent Council said the signs in place complied with Department for Transport guidelines, but that it had decided to install extra lower-level signs and gateway features to give more clarity to drivers.

In the 21 months the scheme has been in place, the north-west London council has collected £54,799 on average per month, with the scheme only in place during term time.

School Streets are being trialled across the borough to enforce road closures during drop-off and pick-up times, policed by CCTV cameras and mobile enforcement teams. Those caught face a PCN of £160, reduced to £80 if paid within 14 days.

Previously, it was reported that 70,000 PCNs were issued in 12 months, at a rate of 384 per school day.

In July 2025, the two cameras enforcing the scheme outside Manor School raised more than £107,000 in a single month, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service .

Want said: "For months I have been highlighting the huge volume of PCNs issued to drivers on the Manor School Street. The fact that it has raked in more than £1m in two years should have told them something wasn't right.

"It is failing children's safety if drivers are still using the road. I fear the scheme is more about revenue generation than improving road safety or air quality."

Promise Knight, the council's cabinet member for cleaner streets, transport and public realm, said School Streets existed in the borough "to make the journey to and from school safer for children and families".

"The purpose of the scheme is to protect children by reducing congestion and improving air quality.

"We will continue to review the scheme and make practical improvements where they can help drivers comply."

articles.title: BJP chief Nitin Nabin asks opposition to follow LK Advani's approach to national security
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying political parties should stand together with the government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security.Speaking at a special event at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi to mark Advani's 100th birthday, Nabin recalled the veteran leader's stand in Parliament when the BJP was in the Opposition.“Whenever he spoke in Parliament, he always said that the BJP will be with the government on issues related to the country's security despite being in the Opposition. As a Leader of the Opposition, he said very clearly that the entire Opposition would be with the government when it came to the country. This is something people need to learn even today,” Nabin said.He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.Nabin recalls Advani's partnership with VajpayeeNabin said Advani and former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had different temperaments and personalities, but their ability to work together towards a common goal was unparalleled.He credited the two leaders with laying the foundation for the BJP's expansion from a party with just two Lok Sabha MPs, saying their determination helped the organisation overcome uncertainty in its early years.“As India moves forward into the 21st century, the Bharatiya Janata Party is also moving ahead with its expansion and development. The BJP is working to take forward both the heritage of this country and the legacy of the party,” he said.Nabin also described Advani as an example of the dignity, probity and sensitivity that politics should uphold.“I could not get an opportunity to work with him, but what I have heard from others who worked with him tells me that Advani's life has been an inspiration for everyone in BJP,” he said.He added that Advani had demonstrated immense dedication to the nation despite having experienced the pain of Partition.“He could take even hard decisions with simplicity,” Nabin said.Ram Rath Yatra and Ayodhya temple recalledRecalling Advani's role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Nabin referred to the veteran leader's Ram Rath Yatra, which was stopped at Samastipur in Bihar.He said the slogan “We will build the temple right there” had been raised by BJP workers and crores of people across the country. Although the yatra was halted in Bihar, kar sevaks carried forward Advani's mission, he said.Nabin credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with taking that journey forward, pointing to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a moment to remember Advani's contribution.“Today, as the country witnesses the magnificent Shri Ram Temple standing in Ayodhya, it is a moment for all of us to honour and remember Shri Advani Ji's historic journey,” he said.Piyush Goyal recalls personal associationSenior Union minister and BJP treasurer Piyush Goyal also recalled his association with Advani, saying the veteran leader never made others feel the weight of his seniority or influence.He said party workers fondly called Advani 'dada' and that the leader had always treated him like a family member, addressing him by his nickname, 'Happy'.“Advani only thought about taking the country and taking the party forward with complete selflessness,” Goyal said, while wishing him a long life.“We all wish that this country continues to get a leader like Lal Krishna Advani,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Former Palestinian detainees at mercy of Israel amid perpetual detention
articles.summary: Former Palestinian detainees in the West Bank are being repeatedly detained by Israeli forces, affecting their families.
articles.body:
Ahmed Abed (a pseudonym due to ongoing threats of arrest) still feels like a prisoner despite being released from an Israeli jail to the occupied West Bank nearly two years ago.

Despite being technically “free”, Abed, 43, is still often rearrested by Israeli forces or summoned by intelligence for interrogation.

Hundreds of other Palestinians in the occupied West Bank face similar ordeals after being released from Israeli prisons. Their homes are sometimes raided twice a week; they can be detained, assaulted and interrogated on the spot before being released.

Every day, organisations dedicated to prisoners’ affairs document the arrests of dozens of Palestinians across the West Bank as part of large-scale operations that frequently target former detainees. Most of those detained are released after hours of interrogation, in what appears to be a campaign of intimidation by Israel against former Palestinian prisoners.

Abed was released as part of a prisoner exchange deal between Hamas and Israel in January 2025, having served 22 years of a life sentence. Since his release, he has faced persistent harassment by the Israeli military.

Just days after Abed’s release, he was summoned by Israeli intelligence for questioning. They informed him that they were unhappy with the political decision to carry out the exchange deal and warned they would rearrest him if he made the “slightest mistake”.

Since his release, he has been arrested six times and summoned for interrogation five times. Each time, his home has been raided and his family terrorised by Israeli soldiers. His father was once arrested simply because Abed happened to be outside his house at night.

“Whenever there are reports of Israeli military activity in the city, my family goes into a state of high alert; no one sleeps all night,” he told Al Jazeera. “Some neighbours even leave their homes, fearing they might be raided as part of the collective intimidation campaign imposed because of me.”

When Abed is arrested, he is often forced to walk for several kilometres handcuffed and blindfolded, accompanied by soldiers. He is then placed in a detention centre under dire conditions, deprived of food and water, subjected to beatings and verbal abuse, and then the threats begin.

“Every time, they threaten to send me back to prison to the point where I feel as though two-thirds of my body are still in captivity, with only one-third outside,” he said. “The threats vary, but the underlying message is always the same: I am not permitted to do anything ordinary or live a normal life like everyone else.”

Abed avoids family gatherings, fearing his presence may bring them harm, and so limits his interactions to his immediate family. An Israeli officer warned him that if he were to go to the mosque to pray, he would be arrested.

“The Israeli officer told me, ‘We have zero patience for you. Any behaviour we deem inappropriate, or any movement we find suspicious, we will rearrest you immediately,’” Abed added.

Although he managed to earn both a bachelor’s degree and a doctorate during his time in prison, he has been unable to secure a job. When employers learn about his repeated arrests, they refuse to hire him. Instead, he has to rely on day-labour work to cover his basic costs.

A former prisoner from Qalqilya says he is arrested on average twice a week during the frequent Israeli military sweeps of the city, where former detainees are targeted. He was recently warned during one interrogation that if he ever set foot on a football pitch, he would be arrested. This puts his job as a referee in jeopardy.

Abdullah, another former prisoner from the city who also requested not to use his real name, told Al Jazeera that he has been arrested so many times since his release in 2000 that he has lost count. But he says he has spent a total of 17 years in custody since his “release”.

He was recently held under “administrative detention”, lasting from November 2023 to February 2025, during which he was subject to physical and psychological torture. By the time he was released, he had lost 60kg (132 pounds).

Abdullah, who supports a family of seven, is repeatedly arrested and released after a few hours, but only after his children have been terrorised and his home ransacked.

His employer grew frustrated with his repeated detentions and found a replacement for him.

“After losing my job, I began working on a piece of land I inherited from my father. However, due to arrests and threats, I can never find the right time to tend to it,” he said. “I often fall behind in irrigating, applying pesticides, or tilling the soil, all of which have taken a toll on my seasonal yields, leaving me with more losses than profits.”

Since the outbreak of the war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023, the occupied West Bank has witnessed a wave of Israeli arrest campaigns and pogroms. Israeli troops now make regular incursions into towns, refugee camps, and homes, as well as arrests at military checkpoints to detain former prisoners.

Palestinian prisoner advocacy organisations have documented approximately 26,000 arrests in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, between October 2023, when the genocidal war on Gaza began, and early October 2026. This figure includes more than 800 women and nearly 2,000 minors. The total encompasses individuals who were subsequently released, not just those who remain in custody.

Amani Sarahneh, a spokesperson for the Palestinian Prisoner’s Society, told Al Jazeera that Israeli operations in the West Bank have evolved into a continuous, round-the-clock wave of detentions. On average, between 10 and 15 Palestinians are arrested and remain in Israeli custody every day.

These arrests not only take place at night, as they did before, but also during daylight hours, at military checkpoints, and through field interrogations.

“The persistence of these campaigns has led to a ‘normalisation of fear’ among the citizens, which has significantly impacted social relations, particularly in villages where residents live in a state of constant anxiety, fearing that occupation forces might storm their towns or public spaces and arrest groups of people at any moment,” she told Al Jazeera.

These arrests are frequently accompanied by physical assaults and abuse, with detainees held for long hours while handcuffed and blindfolded. The victims’ family homes are frequently ransacked and possessions taken away during the Israeli raids.

“These policies also include using family members of those targeted, such as wives and sisters, as hostages to exert pressure,” Sarahneh said.

“The impact of these campaigns has extended beyond the detainees and their families, deepening a sense of fear and apprehension among the general public, who now worry that the arrests could reach a much wider segment of the population,” Sarahneh said.

articles.title: Building owned by Saudi oil giant damaged in missile attack on Riyadh’s financial district
articles.summary: A building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the financial district in the capital Riyadh has been damaged in a missile attack.
articles.body: A building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the financial district of the capital Riyadh has been damaged in a missile attack. The strike in King Abdullah Financial District has been claimed by the Iran-allied Houthis and came after Saudi Civil Defense issued ‌an early-warning ⁠alert of a potential threat to the city. Video circulating on social media and verified by CNN shows damage to several floors of the Aramco building, with windows seen blown out. But Saudi authorities said the impact was minimal. “An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack,” on Sunday, according to the official Saudi news agency, citing a source at the Saudi Energy Ministry. “The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported,” the agency reported. However, one witness said they saw ambulances heading to the area. CNN has reached out to the Information Ministry by email for further details. The Houthis, who have fired missiles and drones towards multiple targets across Saudi Arabia over the last three months, said in the attack on Riyadh’s financial district was one of several it carried out on Aramco targets. There was no initial comment from Saudi authorities on the additional claims. The Houthis said they had also targeted Saudi-led ground forces in several parts of Yemen. The Saudi led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles in Riyadh and the southern region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote in a post on X that air defenses also “intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh.” Saudi defense challenges The missile attacks on Riyadh came a day after Yemen’s Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi airstrikes had ‌killed ‌at least ​33 ​people near the capital Sanaa, including women and children. “We will punish the Saudi regime for its crimes against the Yemeni people,” said Mahdi al-Mashat, a senior Houthi official, on Saturday. Last month, 13 people were killed in one missile strike on Riyadh’s international airport, and several more died in other strikes on the airport. The Houthis have said they will continue firing missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia so long as the Kingdom carries out airstrikes against the parts of Yemen they control and enforces a blockade against its territory. Saudi Arabia spent $83 billion on defense last year, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, putting it firmly among the top ten military spenders worldwide. It has acquired US fighter jets as well as Patriot and THAAD air defense systems, and a range of advanced weaponry from France and the United Kingdom. But the Saudis have a lot to defend: a country roughly one-fifth the size of the US, with threats on three sides - from Iran, Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, and the Houthis. The Saudis are intercepting many of the missiles and drones fired by the Houthis. But some get through. The defense ministry faces difficult choices in distributing the existing systems with so many installations vulnerable to attack. The Houthis have learned to combine ballistic and cruise missiles with long-range drones to overwhelm Saudi defenses, according to analysts. In Yemen, the Saudi-backed coalition is trying to prevent the Houthis from advancing further south towards the port of Aden, which is held by the internationally-recognized government. The Houthis have frequently targeted Aden’s airport with missiles in recent weeks, after taking a stretch of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in September. Hostilities between the Houthis, who are backed by Iran, and Saudi Arabia reignited in July, shattering a 2022 UN-brokered ceasefire that had largely halted fighting ⁠between the ‌two sides. Ibrahim Dahman, Teele Rebane and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.

articles.title: A New York bank filed to foreclose on a married couple's home, missed a 2017 court deadline and let its case be dismissed in 2019; after waiting more than six years to revive the case, it lost another appeal
articles.summary: A New York bank has failed in its attempt to restart a home foreclosure case after allowing it to remain inactive for more than six years.
articles.body: A New York bank has failed in its attempt to restart a home foreclosure case after allowing it to remain inactive for more than six years. The bank had started legal proceedings against a married couple over their home in Sullivan County, New York, but missed a deadline set by the court in 2017. The case was eventually dismissed in 2019.Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas had approached the court after an alleged default on a loan taken by David A. Leis. The loan was secured by a mortgage on a residential property signed by Leis and his wife, Marie Leis.According to the ruling, as part of the foreclosure proceedings, the court directed the bank in March 2017 to file a required application by December 31 that year. It also warned the bank that the case could be removed from the court calendar if it missed the deadline. If the bank did not take steps to bring the case back within a year, it could be dismissed.The bank failed to submit the application on time. In January 2018, the court informed it that the case had been removed from the calendar. The bank then missed another opportunity to act. It did not ask the court to restart the case within the next year.As a result, the court dismissed the foreclosure case on January 7, 2019. The dismissal was without prejudice, meaning the court did not rule on the merits of the bank's foreclosure claim.However, the bank did not approach the court again until February 2025. It asked for the dismissal to be cancelled and the case to be restored to the active list. The court rejected the request in April 2025, prompting the bank to appeal.On Thursday, the New York Supreme Court's Appellate Division, Third Department, upheld that decision. The judges said the bank had not given a convincing explanation for failing to meet the deadline or for waiting more than six years to challenge the dismissal.Bank could not explain why it missed deadlinesThe appellate court noted that the bank had been clearly warned about what would happen if it failed to meet the December 2017 deadline. Despite this, it neither filed the required application nor asked the court for more time.The bank also failed to act after receiving the January 2018 notice that the case had been removed from the calendar. It then allowed the matter to remain inactive until February 2025 before asking the court to reopen it.The judges said the bank had not provided an affidavit from its lawyer or any other person with direct knowledge of the case. Such a statement could have explained why the deadline was missed, why the bank did not respond to the court's notice and why it took so long to seek the restoration of the case.The bank referred to earlier court decisions in which mistakes made by lawyers or their offices had been accepted as reasons for missing deadlines. However, the judges said the bank had not identified any such mistake.It did not point to a specific error in recording the deadline, a communication problem within the law office or any other incident that could explain its failure to act. It also gave no reason for waiting more than six years to challenge the dismissal.Court rejects bank's other argumentsThe bank also argued that the couple had not filed a notice of entry for the 2019 dismissal order. It suggested that this was relevant to the delay in seeking to reopen the case.The appellate court disagreed. It said the notice of entry affected the time available to file a request to cancel the dismissal. However, it did not explain why the bank had failed to follow the court's earlier directions or provide a reasonable reason for its prolonged inaction.The judges said the lower court was justified in rejecting the bank's request because it had failed to explain its conduct.They also said there was no need to examine whether the bank had a valid foreclosure claim. Before considering that question, the bank first had to explain why it had missed the deadlines. Since it failed to do so, the court did not need to examine the strength of its original case.The bank further argued that the lower court should have used its authority to reopen the matter in the interest of justice. articles.summary: KANPUR: Three members of a family, including a 20-day-old baby, died when the roof of their house collapsed on Diwali morning in Kanpur’s Panki Padaav
articles.body: KANPUR: Three members of a family, including a 20-day-old baby, died when the roof of their house collapsed on Diwali morning in Kanpur’s Panki Padaav area. A fourth family member suffered minor injuries.The roof collapsed on Sunday morning, trapping Vinodni Shukla (60), her son Harsh Shukla (32), daughter-in-law Anshika Shukla (28) and grandson Aarav under debris.Family members and neighbours pulled them out and took them to Kalyanpur CHC, where doctors declared Vinodni, Anshika and Aarav dead. Harsh survived with minor injuries.The four were in a mud room when its roof, made of bamboo supports and mud, collapsed.Anshika was breastfeeding Aarav at the time. Neighbours said she apparently tried to protect the child by holding him tightly beneath her, but both died.The 35-year-old single-storey ancestral house, comprising four rooms, belongs to Avdhesh Shukla (65). He and his younger son, Raju Shukla (29), were in another room when the accident occurred.Harsh works for a Steel Authority company in Panki and had married Anshika two years ago. Their son was born 20 days before the accident.After doctors declared the three dead, the family brought their bodies home and initially refused to allow postmortems. Police later persuaded them to consent.DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said, “Information was received about the death of 3 people after the roof of a house collapsed. Prima facie, it appears that the load on the roof increased due to water seepage. For now, the bodies are being sent for postmortem. A revenue team is also present at the spot. articles.title: A once-storied ocean liner is getting a new life as the world’s largest artificial reef
articles.summary: A once-famous ocean liner makes its final voyage to join the Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail as an artificial reef and scuba destination.
articles.body: A storied American ocean liner that once set a world record crossing the sea is about to set one beneath it. This month, a series of explosions will blow holes in the former SS United States, sinking it some 25 miles off the Florida panhandle to become the world’s largest artificial reef. When it hits the sand some 180 feet below the surface, the massive ocean liner will become the 21st and largest vessel on the Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail, spanning the roughly 150-mile coastline from Pensacola to Port St. Joe. The trail, with shipwrecks dating back to 1942, has become a haven for both marine life and recreational scuba divers since its official establishment in 2012 — an effort to boost tourism after the devastating 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill. The sinking will give new life to a vessel whose once-striking black-and-red exterior paint has been faded by the sun as rust spots pockmark a hull that ferried American luminaries and European royals across the Atlantic Ocean. Besides plans to use the ship as a dive site, the SS United States Conservancy, a nonprofit that has been taking care of the ship and preserving its history, plans to eventually build a museum in Florida near dive embarkation sites where visitors can see artifacts from the vessel and explore its history. The ship’s two large funnels have been removed and are expected to be part of the museum. Transatlantic king The SS United States was more than a luxury passenger ship. At 990-feet – larger than the Titanic — and with a top speed of 44 mph set during sea trials, it was also considered a military asset, so much so that when construction began in 1950, its more than $70 million cost was divided among the Transportation Department’s Maritime Administration, the US Navy and the commercial United States Lines, according to the Naval Historical Foundation. The ship was designed so that it could quickly be converted for troop transport, with its normal complement of 1,900 to 2,000 passengers replaced by up to 14,000 troops. And its maiden voyage in 1952 saw it cross the Atlantic from New York to Europe in just under three days and 11 hours at about 42 mph — a record that stands to this day. Largely made of aluminum to conserve weight, SS United States was about 10 mph faster than today’s cruise ships, which have more steel construction. During its heyday in the 1950s and 1960s, it was the most prestigious way to cross the Atlantic. Four sitting, retired or future US presidents sailed on it: Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy and Bill Clinton. International and Hollywood royalty — including Marlon Brando, Sean Connery, Marilyn Monroe, Judy Garland, Prince Rainer of Monaco and the Duke and Duchess of Windsor, among others — used its staterooms. Maritime historian Sal Mercogliano called the ship “the culmination of a centuries-long race to conquer the North Atlantic and bridge Europe and North America.” But its reign as king of the Atlantic would not last long. “Its fate was sealed in 1958 with the introduction of the commercial jet liner which replaced the ocean liner as the primary means to cross the Atlantic,” said Mercogliano, a professor at Campbell University in North Carolina. It was retired in 1969. “Her sinking will mark the end of the great ocean liners,” Mercogliano said. A home for the fishes In the years after its retirement, the SS United States sat at a few Atlantic ports as a succession of owners decided what to do with it. In 2024, with it facing eviction from the Philadelphia shipyard where it had been tied up for 30 years, owners faced a choice: sell it for scrap or sell it to become an artificial reef. It was then that Okaloosa County, Florida, stepped in with a $1 million bid to buy it, according to the county’s website. Last year, after several delays, the ship was towed the 1,800 miles from Philadelphia to Mobile, Alabama, where it was stripped of any hazardous materials that could harm the marine environment. Most of the ship’s interior was gutted before that trip, according to the conservancy. Remarkably, the ship’s hull retains 90% of its original integrity, the conservancy’s website said. “The ship’s hull was designed similar to battleship specifications and was built to stand the test of time, surpassing today’s cruise ships,” it said. That should serve it well at the bottom of the Gulf, where it is expected to quickly become the center of a thriving ecosystem, marine scientists said. “Fishes will start congregating around a new artificial reef within hours or days,” said Michael Parsons, professor of marine science at Florida Gulf Coast University in Fort Myers, adding that bacteria and algae will make the SS United States their home almost immediately. According to the diving trail’s website, previous wrecks have attracted large numbers of fish like snapper, grouper, amberjack, angelfish and barracuda as well as sea urchin and corals. Artificial reefs offer marine life protection, scientists said. “In the open ocean, having hiding spots or things to grow on can increase survival, so they can serve as nurseries or population refuges for some species, particularly fish,” said Melissa May, associate professor of marine biology at FGCU. While the ship is expected to quickly attract marine life, measuring its effectiveness depends on the reason it was deployed, said Chris Stallings, a professor of biological oceanography at the University of South Florida in Tampa. “Artificial reefs are tools, not inherently good or bad solutions. The question is, what ‘problem’ are we trying to solve with them?” he asked. Some may be designed to make fishing easier, others to make the overall ecosystem more abundant, he said. Okaloosa County is touting the SS United States as an environmental and economic boost. If it can bring divers to the region and drive tourism, it will have a benefit outside the ocean, Stallings said. “Artificial reefs can support recreational fishing, charter fishing businesses, dive charter operations, boat and fuel sales, as well as hotels, lodging, and restaurants for tourists visiting the area to enjoy activities associated with the reefs,” he said. If it lands on the Gulf floor upright, the keel of the SS United States will sit at a depth of 180 feet, but the ship’s large size means it’s upper deck could be just 55 to 60 feet below the surface, making it accessible to recreational divers with open-water certification, according to the Okaloosa County Tourism Department website. Once sunk, the SS United States will surpass its predecessors on the trail, including a sunken aircraft carrier, the former USS Oriskany, by nearly 80 feet. “Get ready to explore a record-breaking ship, now repurposed, reborn and soon to be breaking records in the underwater world,” it says.
